newsitem.title: JORDAN: Russia wants comprehensive Arab-Israeli talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants comprehensive Arab-Israeli talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov called on Sunday for resumption of comprehensive Middle East peace talks, saying individual breakthroughs would falter unless Arabs and Israelis made across-the-board progress.
"There is a need to have talks on all tracks at one time," Primakov told a news conference in Jordan at the end of a week-long Middle East tour.
"Whatever achievement is made on one track, it could regress if there isn't progress on the others," he said, speaking through an interpreter.
International attention has focused on Israeli and Palestinian negotiations for a long-overdue Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
But Primakov said his trip, which took him to Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Egypt, the Palestinian territories and Jordan, had focused on defusing tension between Israel and Syria.

"There was special attention during this trip to the Syrian-Israeli track. This is not by chance," he said. "Russia sees its task as a joint sponsor of the peace process to end the tension between Israel and Syria in this situation."

Five years of peace talks between the two countries are stuck over the Golan Heights, captured by Israel from Syria in the 1967 Middle East War. Israeli talks with Lebanon, where Syria is the main power broker, are dependent on progress on the Syrian front.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, elected in May, has rejected returning Arab land in return for peace and in recent weeks Israeli and Syrian officials have accused each other of beating the drums of war.
Primakov said he had passed on assurances from both sides that neither was planning any aggressive military action.
"Russia will continue its plan for mediating in the border issues," he added.
He said the two principles that guided talks during his tour of the region were a need for negotiations on all tracks, and a commitment to implementing agreements already signed.

Palestinians say Netanyahu is trying to change agreements signed by his predecessor Shimon Peres -- including withdrawal from Hebron -- and to renege on the principle of land for peace enshrined in the 1991 Middle East peace conference in Madrid.
Primakov said Russia, one of the two co-sponsors of the Madrid process along with the United States, was not competing with other mediators.

"We came to the region at a time when the peace process is in crisis," Primakov said. "Russia is not opposing any plans by other parties...(The peace process) needs coordinated efforts from all sides."
"There is a realistic basis for optimism (but) it is not excessive optimism, because things do not progress easily," Primakov said.
